headline: St. Pete Seeks Injunction Against Tire Shop Amid Dengue Outbreak
summary: St. Petersburg filed an injunction against a used tire shop, Thach Tire & Rim, arguing it was a sanitary nuisance, after residents in the Euclid-St. Paul area urged the city to address dengue. The story would investigate whether legal action against suspected mosquito breeding sites is an effective and fair way to curb a local dengue outbreak, and what evidence links the shop to cases.
solution: Using a court injunction to force a property owner to eliminate suspected mosquito breeding sites
location: Euclid-St. Paul area, St. Petersburg, Pinellas County, Florida

fact_checks.reason: 3 of 6 claims confirmed; 3 partly confirmed; mixed evidence on whether it works.

headline: Singapore's Wolbachia Mosquito Program Hits 53% of Homes: What Do Results Show?
summary: Project Wolbachia, Singapore's mosquito-release program to control dengue, now covers more than half of households a decade after it began. The story would examine what the published research and case trends show, what the program costs, and which areas remain uncovered. It would also test officials' warning that the fight against mosquitoes must continue.
solution: Releasing male mosquitoes infected with Wolbachia bacteria so that eggs do not hatch and the mosquito population shrinks
location: Singapore (including Ang Mo Kio and Tampines)

headline: Can Cemetery Flower Rules Curb Dengue Mosquito Breeding on All Souls' Day?
summary: A Brazilian regional news article says flower arrangements on graves can hold standing water and help dengue mosquitoes breed around Dia de Finados (All Souls' Day). A biologist explains precautions for visitors. The story would investigate whether cemetery-focused precautions are being promoted or enforced, and whether they reduce breeding sites.
solution: Public guidance on handling grave flowers and vases to avoid standing water
